source_review: RetentionSource interface excludes value, text, query and gold capabilities.
Retention receives only previous active metadata, causal actual cold-hit admissions, new arrivals, past actual read ledger, epoch and seed.
Each arm has a separate access ledger; pending cold hits are admitted only at the next epoch for quota policies.
Future full-bank search indexing is present; visible-pool scoring and the executed future perturbation check bound its observed use.
Gold is not passed to retention, retrieval or packet reader; scoring starts after closing the complete source-only trial stream.
Four-call fallback is based on source-only reader status or a fixed scheduled cold allocation, with shared rendered-byte budget.
Global search pages unseen source IDs; renamed path metadata and future body perturbations are separately constructed fixtures.
Final BM25 terms are sorted before floating accumulation to remove hash-seed iteration ambiguity.
scope_limits: Eight engineered workload overlays share a common backbone and are not independent causal mechanisms or structurally held-out data.
All sources, clean metadata, project/key scopes and dependency links are supplied; downstream reader interprets structured ASSERT records.
Latest policies intentionally ignore expiry during retention and can lose an older base or historical version.
Indexing is built from the full bank; this is logical temporal selection, not OS-isolated incremental index construction.
Candidate and term counters omit multiple maintenance/indexing/runtime operations and cannot establish end-to-end speed.
No actual full collection, output audit, figure validation, natural-history replication or LLM-reader success was accepted by this precollection review.
